opportunities.title: One agent-readable front door: board proposal intake, resident work-order intake, tap-to-call, owned domain, claimed Google profile
opportunities.problem: Every revenue and service interaction with this firm starts as a phone call inside a 9:00-4:30 weekday window or as a hand-typed free-text email, and the firm's two public identities (Weebly subdomain vs the parked branded domain) plus an unclaimed 1.6-star Google profile make it hard to find, read, trust or transact with - including for AI assistants, since nothing is bookable or submittable online.
evidence: Proposal requests can only be phoned in or sent as a hand-written email containing 11 fields (association name, address, contact, daytime phone, units, property type, current manager, board status, special requirements); there is no form element on the page (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/proposal-request.html)

Resident work orders use the same pattern - call (732) 828-7200 or email a template with name, street address, phones, association, manager and issue description - and emergencies are routed to the same number (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/submit-a-work-order.html)

Contact page has zero form elements and zero tel: links (phone is plain text), so a mobile visitor cannot tap to call, and the home page shows no phone number at all (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/contact-us.html)
Staffed hours are Mon-Fri 9:00-4:30 with Friday closing at 3:00 between Memorial Day and Labor Day (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/contact-us.html)

The branded domain mpm-nj.com serves a GoDaddy parking lander, while the City of Long Branch business directory still lists mpm-nj.com as the firm's web address - two identities, one dead end (https://mpm-nj.com/lander)

Google Business Profile at 315 Raritan Ave is unclaimed ('Claim this business'), publishes no hours ('Add hours'), shows 1.6 stars, and links the free Weebly subdomain; no owner responses are visible (https://www.google.com/maps/search/Midlantic+Property+Management+315+Raritan+Ave+Highland+Park+NJ)

Site is on a free Weebly subdomain with a 2013 footer, no h1, no meta description, no JSON-LD, and a header slideshow that renders blank at desktop and at 390px phone width (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/)

Context only, not this firm: a vendor secret-shop of 100 other property management companies found 51% did not answer during 9-5 weekday hours and 1% returned a missed call (vendor study, leasing segment, low strength) (https://www.hiresuper.com/resources/we-called-100-property-managers-at-narpm-most-didnt-answer)
opportunities.agent_design: Three parts, shipped behind one intake layer. (1) Front-door repair: claim the Google profile and publish hours/service list; put the site on the owned domain (or 301 the parked domain to the real site); add LocalBusiness/Organization JSON-LD with service towns and counties, real tel: links, an h1 and meta descriptions; make the service and proposal pages static-rendered text so Googlebot, OAI-SearchBot and PerplexityBot can read terms, hours and service area. (2) Proposal-intake agent: a conversational form (and an equivalent inbound-phone flow) that captures the 11 fields already listed on the proposal page, checks whether the association sits in the firm's service counties, asks two or three qualifying questions (unit count, property type, current manager, board timeline), and produces a structured intake record plus a one-page briefing for the president - no auto-sent proposal. (3) Resident request form that classifies routine vs emergency and hands emergency to a person or on-call line immediately. Triggers: form submit, inbound call, inbound email to the general office address. Human approves: any outbound proposal, pricing or commitment, and the site/GBP publish step; the agent drafts, the president or a manager sends.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: A form builder fixes the form but not the chain: domain and redirect work, Google profile claim plus structured data that AI assistants and Googlebot actually parse, a qualifying agent that routes to the right person without promising management terms, and an intake record that lands as structured data instead of another email in one shared inbox. Doing this without an agent leaves the 4:30 p.m. and summer-Friday gaps and the second dead domain exactly as they are.

impact_estimate.range: $6k-$14k/yr of recovered admin time (5-8 hrs/week of re-keying proposal and work-order emails into structured records), plus board inquiries that today cannot arrive after 4:30 p.m. or before 9:00 a.m. at all - unmonetized because the firm publishes no inquiry or portfolio data
impact_estimate.assumptions: Uses the NJ median wage for Secretaries and Administrative Assistants (except legal, medical, executive), $50,260/yr = about $24.16/hr, loaded to roughly $31/hr with an assumed 28% for benefits and overhead. Assumes the single shared office inbox plus the open part-time AR/admin role absorb that re-keying volume, and that about half of it moves to a form/agent. Recovery is stated as time value, not revenue: applying the vendor missed-call percentages to Midlantic would be an extrapolation from a different segment (leasing) and is deliberately excluded from the dollar range.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 2-3 weeks: claimed Google profile with hours and services; site on the owned domain with the parked domain 301'd (or, if the domain cannot be recovered, the Weebly subdomain hardened); LocalBusiness JSON-LD, tel: links, h1/meta descriptions and an AI-readable service/proposal page; a live proposal-intake form that emails a structured record and a briefing note to the president with auto-acknowledgement; a resident work-order form with emergency flagging; a before/after read-out of what an assistant can now find, answer and submit.

opportunities.title: 24/7 work-order triage and dispatch agent across associations, trades and the after-hours operator line
opportunities.problem: All resident requests and emergencies land on one phone number and one general inbox, then get re-keyed by hand; after 4:30 p.m. (3:00 p.m. Fridays in summer) a third-party live operator takes facts by phone and arranges dispatch, with no resident self-service, no ticket the resident can see, and no reliable audit trail of what was promised to whom.
evidence: Work orders and emergencies share one intake path: call (732) 828-7200 or email a free-text template; the page states emergencies go to the same number (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/submit-a-work-order.html)

The firm says associates are on call 24/7, that after-hours calls are answered by a live operator who 'takes the facts' and arranges dispatch, and that it runs an in-house emergency response team (ERT) that drills at managed sites (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/emergency-procedures.html)
Office hours are 9:00-4:30 Mon-Fri with Friday closing at 3:00 in summer, so a large share of resident contact falls outside staffed hours (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/contact-us.html)

Dispatch spans many trades across the portfolio - electrical, landscaping, elevators, roofs, HVAC, plumbing, boilers, pools, trash, gutter and lighting (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/property-management.html)

The open part-time Administrative/Accounts Receivable Assistant role ($20/hour) is scoped to answering calls, relaying messages, drafting correspondence and helping managers track projects, with Enumerate Central experience preferred - i.e. the ticket system is fed by human re-keying (https://www.indeed.com/q-part-time-property-management-l-east-orange%2C-nj-jobs.html)

Public complaint themes are service-or-repair handling and communication follow-through; one BBB complaint (Jul 2026) is recorded as unresolved and another (Aug 2025) as unanswered (https://www.bbb.org/us/nj/highland-park/profile/property-management/midlantic-property-management-0221-12002517/complaints)

Benchmark: access to a generative-AI assistant raised issues resolved per hour by 14% on average across 5,179 customer support agents, with a 34% gain for novices (NBER working paper 31161, published in QJE 2025) - the closest measured analogue for high-volume request handling (https://www.nber.org/papers/w31161)
opportunities.agent_design: An intake-and-dispatch agent sitting in front of Enumerate Central. Triggers: web form, inbound email to the office address, the after-hours operator handing off a call summary, and SMS/voice where the association has opted in. On each trigger the agent extracts unit/association/vendor/problem, matches the association to its own SOP and vendor roster, classifies emergency vs routine against written criteria (no heat, no water, active leak, elevator entrapment, lockout, sewer backup), de-duplicates against open tickets for the same unit or building, opens or updates the ticket, sends the resident an acknowledgement with a ticket number and expected response window, and dispatches the on-call vendor or ERT with the access details. Routine items queue for the community manager with a proposed vendor and scope. Exceptions - cost above a set threshold, safety incidents, anything needing board notification, anything the agent cannot classify confidently - go to the on-call human with a summary and the relevant SOP excerpt. Voice handling discloses that the caller is speaking to an AI and offers a person; no outbound automated calls (the FCC's 2024 AI-voice proceeding proposes disclosure and consent duties for AI-generated calls, so outbound stays human-approved). Daily digest to each community manager; monthly volume-by-trade and response-time report for boards. Human approves: vendor commitment above threshold, any board-visible communication, and emergency escalation decisions.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: This is not a chatbot answering FAQs. It has to write into a system of record (Enumerate Central, whose public API surface is unconfirmed from outside - integration may need RPA or structured-email parsing), hold per-association vendor rosters and emergency criteria, enforce response clocks, hand off cleanly to a third-party answering service and an in-house ERT, and leave an audit trail that survives a board meeting or a complaint. Each association's rules differ, so tuning and monitoring is ongoing work, not a one-off setup.

impact_estimate.range: $3.7k-$15k/yr in net intake and dispatch admin time (roughly 20-80 staff hours per month at gross, of which 50-70% is assumed recoverable), plus faster and traceable after-hours dispatch, which is the complaint theme today but is not monetized here
impact_estimate.assumptions: Loads the NJ median Secretary/Administrative Assistant wage of $50,260/yr (about $24.16/hr, roughly $31/hr loaded) for intake work, and applies the NBER working paper's 14% per-hour output gain only as a ceiling check, not as a forecast. The 20-80 hours/month volume is an explicit assumption: the firm publishes no portfolio unit count, so total request volume is unknown and the low end is the number to quote. Savings are gross staff-time value, not headcount reduction - the open part-time role signals the back office is capacity-constrained, so recovered hours likely go to unstarted work rather than to a layoff.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 3-4 weeks on one or two named associations and their 3-4 most common trades (plumbing, HVAC, elevator, water intrusion): intake form plus email parsing into a ticket queue; written emergency criteria per association; automated acknowledgements with ticket numbers; dispatch messages to the existing vendor list; a manager dashboard showing open tickets, age and after-hours volume; measured baseline vs pilot on time-to-acknowledge, duplicate tickets and spread of requests across staffed vs unstaffed hours.

opportunities.title: Delinquency and ledger-dispute agent: assessment-to-lien ladder with per-association policy and a hard human approval gate
opportunities.problem: Delinquency handling is a documented, rules-heavy monthly ladder - 30-day notice, interest, late charges, lien notice, potential foreclosure - run by a small AR/bookkeeping back office, and it is exactly where the firm's public complaints concentrate: residents alleging late fees were not corrected, no ledger was supplied, and a repair-related charge was pursued after communication stopped.
evidence: The FAQ documents the collections workflow: monthly assessments, a 30-day delinquency stage, interest and late charges, lien notices and potential foreclosure for non-payment (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/faqs.html)
Back office carries AP, AR, staff accountant and community-administrator roles together, with no dedicated collections analyst (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/career-opportunities.html)

Current hiring is a part-time Administrative/Accounts Receivable Assistant at $20/hour, i.e. the AR gap is being filled with junior part-time capacity (https://www.indeed.com/q-part-time-property-management-l-east-orange%2C-nj-jobs.html)

BBB records 2 complaints in 3 years against the Highland Park address on 'Order Issues' (Aug 2025, marked unanswered) and 'Service or Repair Issues' (Jul 2026, marked unresolved), and rates the firm D+, not accredited (https://www.bbb.org/us/nj/highland-park/profile/property-management/midlantic-property-management-0221-12002517/complaints)

Complaint content as summarized at BBB alleges delinquency information and late fees were not corrected and no ledger was supplied - an allegation, not a finding, but it describes a ledger-reconciliation failure mode (https://www.bbb.org/us/nj/highland-park/profile/property-management/midlantic-property-management-0221-12002517/complaints)
Benchmark: NJ median wage for Bookkeeping, Accounting and Auditing Clerks is $58,300 (25th $48,400, 75th $67,270) (https://www.onetonline.org/link/localwages/43-3031.00?st=NJ)
opportunities.agent_design: A two-headed agent over the accounting system of record, both with approval gates. (a) Collections ladder: on assessment posting and on each payment-file reconciliation, the agent recomputes each unit's balance, applies that association's own collection policy (bylaws/collection resolution kept as the agent's document set - the knowledge layer), and drafts the correct stage artefact - statement of account, 30-day delinquency letter, interest and late-charge calculation, lien-referral package. It checks arithmetic, prior notices sent, payment plans and disputes on file, and refuses to advance a stage where a dispute is open. (b) Ledger-dispute responder: when a resident, board member or the answering service raises a charge question, the agent assembles the ledger, payment history, policy clause and prior correspondence into a draft reply with an audit trail, and logs a response deadline. Every lien referral, fee waiver, correction and outbound letter is queued for a named human (community manager or controller) to approve; nothing goes to a lien or foreclosure stage without explicit sign-off. Also enforces a first-response SLA on inbound complaints - the failure visible in the BBB record - and escalates open items on a fixed clock. Human approves: all money-touching correspondence, all fee corrections, all lien referrals.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: The arithmetic is auditable money math driven by per-association policy documents that differ from client to client, tied to an accounting system of record, with a legal consequence at the lien stage. A general chatbot cannot hold the policies, cannot recompute a ledger, cannot prove which version of a policy produced which fee, and cannot leave the approval trail a board or a court may ask for. Reliability and privacy here (resident PII, bank data, owner financials) mean private deployment and logging, not a SaaS chat widget.

impact_estimate.range: $5k-$17k/yr in bookkeeping/AR time (roughly 20-40 hours per month of ledger pulls, late-fee recalculation and notice drafting at $36-$38/hr loaded), plus fewer disputed charges and a defensible audit trail on every fee and lien step - not monetized because complaint and escalation counts are only partially visible (2 public BBB complaints in 3 years)
impact_estimate.assumptions: Loads the NJ median Bookkeeping/Accounting/Auditing Clerk wage of $58,300/yr (about $28.03/hr, roughly $36/hr at an assumed 28% for benefits and overhead). The 20-40 hours/month figure is an assumption in the absence of any published portfolio unit count or delinquency rate; if the firm manages 20-40 associations the low end is the defensible number. Excluded: foreclosure-related legal cost avoidance, which would require per-association data the firm does not publish. Do not present this as a revenue-recovery estimate - no arrears data is public.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 3-4 weeks on one cooperative association: ingest its collection policy and bylaws into the knowledge layer; run a historical replay against the last 6-12 months of its payment data to show where the agent's recalculation matches or diverges from what was issued; produce draft 30-day letters and a standard statement-of-account format for human sign-off; stand up the ledger-question draft responder with a response clock; deliver a reconciliation report listing every divergence found so the firm sees the error rate before committing.

lead_score.rationale: Pain evidence is unusually concrete and directly observed rather than inferred: no form element anywhere on the site, zero tel: links, a parked branded domain that a city directory still publishes as their address, an unclaimed Google profile with no hours at 1.6 stars and no visible owner responses, a fax-only hiring page, a single phone-plus-email intake for proposals, work orders and emergencies, and BBB records showing one unanswered and one unresolved complaint. That maps cleanly onto A (work-order dispatch, collections) and G (front door), with C embedded as the policy layer and F as the natural retainer - hence a high fit score. Ability to pay is real but not generous: recurring management fees across Middlesex, Monmouth and Ocean county communities and a $44,931.80 municipal pass-through payment in 2025 show revenue, while a 2013-era free Weebly site, a $20/hour part-time hire and fax-based recruiting show a low technology appetite and a small back office, so this is a 5-figure first engagement, not a transformation budget. Ease is mid: the front-door fix is genuinely fast and the decision-maker is one named president (H. James Polos, who signs the About page), but there is no in-house technical owner, the system of record (Enumerate Central) may have no usable API from outside, and the buyer is the president of a firm whose public posture suggests he is not an early adopter. Strategic value is high: New Jersey has a large population of community associations managed by small firms with the identical shape - phone-and-email intake, per-association policy, monthly delinquency ladder - so a packaged 'association management back office' built here is repeatable. Physical/edge (E) was considered and deliberately left out of the top 3: profile.json shows real physical signals (elevators, boilers, pools, HVAC, 24/7 emergency response), but Midlantic does not own those buildings - each association board owns its site and its capital budget, so a sensor or camera install would be a per-property sale to a separate buyer with a multi-board approval cycle, which cannot be piloted inside one engagement. An E design here would also touch security/surveillance, pulling it into N.J.S.A. 45:5A-2 alarm-business licensing, for a firm that has not yet fixed its own front door. Recommend revisiting E after a first A/G win, scoped to operations monitoring (boiler/water-intrusion/temperature) rather than security, with a licensed contractor installing.

best_evidence_signal: Proposal requests and resident work orders are still phone-only or hand-typed-email-only, and the domain the City of Long Branch still lists as the firm's web address is a GoDaddy parking page (https://mpm-nj.com/lander), while the live site is a 2013-era free Weebly subdomain with zero forms and zero tel: links (https://mpm-nj.weebly.com/proposal-request.html)
